correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID 11674
correspondence.finding: The eastern selected beginning lies in the marsh/interior setting south of Anajás. The originals show Igarapé Fundo joining an unnamed branch, and farther west the Pau-rosa/Braço do Mapuá setting, Lagoa dos Patos, Lagoa do Socó and Braço do Socó connecting toward the Mapuá near Jupati. They do not establish the entire selected east-to-west feeder or its continuous connection into this lake corridor. This is a material source gap rather than a demand for bank/vertex agreement. No name is assigned to the unestablished initial reach; Mapuá is not extended indiscriminately over the lakes or unnamed branches.
correspondence.correspondence: partial; material source/connector gap remains

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID 11675
correspondence.finding: From the Jupati/Nazaré portion the route follows the mapped Mapuá northward through the Vila Amélia/São Pedro sector, then westward to the Aramã joining area near São Vicente. It continues along the northern Aramã arm of the multichannel island complex toward the Jacaré Grande/Companhia/Furo Grande junction. Mapuá-Mirim, Furo dos Macacos and associated island passages are separately shown; they are not all renamed Mapuá or Aramã.
correspondence.correspondence: covered at generalized corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Selected mainstem FID 11676
correspondence.finding: Northward broad Rio Jacaré Grande passage, with the Curumu and Ituquara joining channels and parallel Jacarezinho passage distinguished. The northern selected termination is in the broad waterway beside Ilha das Guaribas, with Ilha Mututi/Limão/Nova nearby. The mapped waterway continues north. Stored terminal class sea is retained as model metadata; it is not evidence that this selected endpoint is an open-ocean mouth or the river’s actual ultimate outlet.
correspondence.correspondence: covered through actual selected terminal

correspondence.component_scope: Selected tributary FID 11677
correspondence.finding: Southwestern approach from the Igarapé Anaticu sector through a small northeastward channel corridor into the Rio Companhia/parallel-furo waterway south of the main junction. The selected model tributary is an approach through the island/channel network; the downstream Jacaré Grande name is not assigned to this entire component. Individual minor-channel equivalences remain unnamed where not secure.
correspondence.correspondence: covered at generalized corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Selected tributary FID 11678
correspondence.finding: Northward Rio Companhia/broad-channel passage alongside the Furo Grande/Jaburu network to the junction where the eastward Aramã–Macacos complex meets the northern Jacaré Grande corridor. The source shows multiple adjacent channels; model tributary role alone does not establish a single river-name scope or flow regime.
correspondence.correspondence: covered through main joining setting

correspondence.component_scope: Initial southeast Sitidgi feeder
correspondence.finding: The headward selection corresponds to the short pond/stream network east of the southern part of Sitidgi Lake and its westward connection to the lake shore. The source shows the small waterbodies, connecting stream and inlet at generalized corridor scale; no hydronym is printed on this selected feeder. The separate larger southern inflow and Williams Lake farther northeast are not substituted for the selected initial approach.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Sitidgi Lake passage
correspondence.finding: From the southeastern inlet setting the selected route traverses the long north–south Sitidgi Lake toward its northern outlet. The original 107B lake outline and label, and DFO Figures 1 and 2, establish the distinct freshwater-lake component south of the estuary.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Sitidgi Creek and southern estuary entry
correspondence.finding: The narrow outlet north of Sitidgi Lake is explicitly labeled Sitidgi Creek on 107B and leads west into the southern elongate Husky Lakes waterbody. DFO pages 3–4 independently describe the shallow creek connection between the freshwater lake and the inland-most estuarine basin. The printed 6 km figure describes that creek in the report, not the selected model length.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Southern basin and northward B1–B2 connection
correspondence.finding: The selected southern estuarine reach runs west then north past the Whale Point/Portage Point setting and through the narrowing west of the island-and-peninsula complex into the larger northern basin. The lake arms and intervening water connection are visible on 107B. DFO Figure 2 places these in the inland B1 and B2 portions of the five-basin estuary; those identifiers are analytical labels, not names for separate rivers.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: B2–B3 throat and southern 107C continuation
correspondence.finding: The selected path continues northeast through the small-channel connection near the adjoining sheet margins into the long middle basin. The original sheets show the narrowing and connected lake-water continuation; the DFO study distinguishes the small channels between B2 and B3 and discusses their influence on mixing. Source evidence supports the material connector without requiring the simplified line to follow an exact bank or island side.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Middle basin, inner fingers and B4 continuation
correspondence.finding: The route runs along the middle basin, turns through the northern ends of the inner-finger channels, and reaches the broad northeastward continuation. Original 107C pixels show the elongate peninsulas, channels and open connecting water. DFO Figure 2 separately identifies B3, the inner fingers and B4, corroborating that the channels form an estuarine link rather than an unnamed gap between isolated lakes.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: B4–B5 basin link and outer-finger approach
correspondence.finding: Original 107D shows the northeastward passage from the lower middle basin into the broad northern/outer basin, followed by the island and peninsula complex of the outer fingers. The map prints Eskimo (Husky) Lakes on this waterbody. DFO Figures 1 and 2 establish the B4/B5 and outer-finger arrangement and the estuarine identity. Generalized line crossings near narrow islands are not used to claim a particular surveyed navigation channel.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal near Thumb Island
correspondence.finding: The final selected approach crosses the northern outer-finger water setting and ends at the opening northwest of Thumb Island, connected to Liverpool Bay. Original 107D shows the connected opening, Thumb Island and Campbell Island, while its wider view labels Liverpool Bay. DFO Figure 1 and pages 3–4 distinguish this marine connection from the southwest inlet called Kugaluk Channel and the Miner and Kugaluk river mouths farther south. The source supports the actual terminal setting at ordinary scale, not a precise modern tidal boundary or mouth vertex.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized component/corridor scale

correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening and initial northwestward course
correspondence.finding: The selected opening southeast of Kangerlussuaq and its initial northwestward course occupy the mapped western Inland Ice. They lie well inland of the ice-free coastal belt.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized geographic component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The ice shading and its contours do not establish a river channel or subglacial flow. No name is assigned to this reach.

correspondence.component_scope: Long middle westward/northwestward inland corridor
correspondence.finding: The long middle route remains within the mapped continental-ice setting while approaching the western margin southeast of Kangerlussuaq. The national original covers the headward/middle area beyond the detailed sheet, and overlaps the detailed sheet at the western approach.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized geographic component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: No continuity of a natural river through or beneath the ice is inferred. The model line is used only for orientation.

correspondence.component_scope: Western ice-margin and northward landward connector
correspondence.finding: The lower approach passes through the ice-margin setting southeast of Kangerlussuaq, with mapped ice lobes, exposed bedrock and surficial-deposit corridors, and turns north into the east–west proglacial valley. Those different terrain classes remain distinct rather than being called one river.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized geographic component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The source establishes the geographic setting throughout this connector; it does not justify equating every modeled interior segment with a surveyed natural channel or glacier outlet. Exact ice fronts and bank positions are not revalidated.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower proglacial valley and neighbouring northern junction
correspondence.finding: The western part of the selected route lies in the broad east–west proglacial/deposit valley immediately north of Tasersuatsiaq and south of the more northerly approach from the Russell-sector valley. The mapped valleys converge beside Kangerlussuaq before reaching the inner fjord. Read primary prose identifies the local main river and northern tributary as Qinnguata Kuussua and Akuliarusiarsuup Kuua respectively.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized geographic component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: The inspected geological map supplies valley/junction geography; the named relationship comes from actually read prose, not from the failed article figure. The northern tributary is context, not an additional selected FID. Neither name is extended to the entire model route.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual terminal at the inner Kangerlussuaq/Søndre Strømfjord head
correspondence.finding: The selected ending is at the proglacial outlet into the innermost Kangerlussuaq/Søndre Strømfjord beside Kangerlussuaq settlement. It is not a termination in Tasersuatsiaq or an onward open-ocean route. The primary prose limits Watson River to the short downstream reach after the tributary/main-river confluence.
correspondence.correspondence: complete at ordinary generalized geographic component/corridor scale
correspondence.limits: Terminal geography and local lower-reach nomenclature are supported at ordinary corridor scale. The model sea-terminal flag alone is not the evidence, and the lower name does not establish a full-length natural river.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern head and Andant–Masurol–Moures country
correspondence.finding: The head lies northeast of Casey and west of Andant, in the La Fortuna–El Silencio/La Primavera country west of Daireaux. Northward it passes the La Tapera, San Alfredo, La Prosperidad and El Camoatí settings, then Moures toward the west side of Salazar. Original topography shows cultivated/plain ground, low rises, broad marsh indications and transport crossings rather than a labeled source river or source lake. The full headward course is visible; no missing connection is being supplied by a nearby name.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete ordinary corridor coverage; mapped ground and marsh setting read, no whole-route watercourse name.

correspondence.component_scope: Salazar to the La Carreta–Albariño corridor
correspondence.finding: North of Salazar the path crosses the El Cautivo and La Victoriana dune/rise country, continues through La Tanita and La Sirena east of La Carreta, and bends northeast into the elongated unnamed marsh/depression around Los Elenos and La Lisa. It then continues toward Albariño and the northeastward railway corridor. The maps distinguish wet hollows from intervening ground; they do not present this mixture as one named river.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete overlapping head and Salazar map coverage, including the large northward bend and local depression passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Albariño–Alagón–Francisco Madero–Pehuajó
correspondence.finding: The line follows the country from Albariño toward El Retiro, crosses the railway southwest of Alagón, passes west of La Catalana and east of 7 de Octubre, then turns northeast through an unnamed elongated lake south of the Francisco Madero–Pehuajó transport corridor near La Martha. It crosses the main road/rail setting east of Francisco Madero and reaches the western/northern side of Pehuajó, beside the southern end of Laguna La Salada. The selected line continues northeast rather than extending up the entire named lake.
correspondence.correspondence: Original Pehuajó panel and regional overview read throughout. Lake passage, intervening plain and city/transport crossings visible; no unseen connector remains.

correspondence.component_scope: Pehuajó–Chiclana–Guanaco lake and interfluve passage
correspondence.finding: Northeast of Pehuajó the selected route crosses alternating low ground and separate elongate lake/depression settings, reaches Chiclana and turns north through country west/northwest of Guanaco (San Bernardo on the 1:250,000 map). It passes the chain of small depressions near San Juan and then bends southeast. The 1:100,000 original clearly shows field divisions, low contours and intervening ground between these depressions, with no continuous named watercourse. The nearby La Cautiva lake label on the overview is not extended to the entire chain.
correspondence.correspondence: Overlapping 1:250,000 and full 1:100,000 detail coverage resolves the local lake/interfluve setting at generalized corridor scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Santo Tomás and western Carlos Casares
correspondence.finding: From the San Juan country the line turns east across the plain north of the Route 5 and railway corridor, passes the Santo Tomás lake/depression setting, and approaches Carlos Casares from the west. It crosses the railway/road corridor on the west side of the city and turns northeast through the marshy strip west/northwest of the urban center. No source map names this entire eastward passage as one river.
correspondence.correspondence: Entire passage read in the Casares and terminal 1:250,000 panels and full overview; no blank area on the selected corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Carlos Casares–Gobernador Arias–Santa Rita northern loop
correspondence.finding: The route proceeds northeast from Carlos Casares through the Las Mercedes/Gobernador Arias setting, along elongated wet depressions toward Santa Rita and north of La María. It then turns east across intervening field/rise ground and additional separate hollows south of the La Catita/La Madrugada country. The north/east loop is geographically visible as several plain and wetland settings, not a single named continuous channel.
correspondence.correspondence: Full 1:250,000 corridor, with 1:100,000 detail over the eastern part. The 1:100,000 white patch farther north is outside the selected route.

correspondence.component_scope: Canal Mercante crossing and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: Near Galo Llorente the final loop turns southeast and crosses the southwest–northeast alignment labeled Canal Mercante on the 1:250,000 map, then turns south and finally east into a separate small unnamed wet depression in the La Escondida–San Vicente country, north of Cambaceres. The 1:100,000 original shows the same corridor as a railway and resolves intervening field/dune ground and the small terminal depression east of La Escondida and north of San Vicente. These historical map depictions are kept distinct; no change date or present hydraulic relationship is inferred. The selected endpoint is beyond the crossing, not a terminus assigned to Canal Mercante.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual ending and its approach read in both original scales. No terminal name or modern operating connection is invented.

correspondence.component_scope: Branch/reservoir scope and provincial drainage context
correspondence.finding: The retained selection consists of one mainstem FID; no separate selected tributary or reservoir passage needs a shared name. Official Carlos Casares EIA prose describes insufficient naturally developed drainage, dunes that obstruct surface runoff, and separate engineered urban drainage facilities. This supports interpretation of the surrounding plain but is not substituted for direct map reading or used to impose a Salado/Quinto/canal name on the selected line.
correspondence.correspondence: All selected geographic components read. Regional prose is contextual only; no uninspected EIA figure supplies cartographic evidence.
